source_text: Ταῖς μὲν ἐκ τῆς φύσεως παρασκευαῖς ἐλαττούμενον, τῇ δὲ τοῦ λόγου περιουσίᾳ πρὸς οὐρανὸν αὐτὸν ὑπεραρθῆναι δυνάμενον. Ἐὰν ταῦτα μάθωμεν, ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιγνωσόμεθα, Θεὸν γνωρίσομεν, τὸν κτίσαντα προσκυνήσομεν, τῷ Δεσπότῃ δουλεύσομεν, τὸν Πατέρα δοξάσομεν, τὸν τροφέα ἡμῶν ἀγαπήσομεν, τὸν εὐεργέτην αἰδεσθησόμεθα, τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἡμῶν τῆς παρούσης καὶ τῆς μελλούσης προσκυνοῦντες οὐκ ἀπολήξομεν, τὸν δι' οὗ παρέσχετο ἤδη πλούτου καὶ τὰ ἐν ἐπαγγελίαις πιστούμενον, καὶ τῇ πεῖρᾳ τῶν παρόντων βεβαιοῦντα ἡμῖν τὰ προσδοκώμενα. Εἰ γὰρ τὰ πρόσκαιρα τοιαῦτα, ποταπὰ τὰ αἰώνια; Καὶ εἰ τὰ ὁρώμενα οὕτω καλὰ, ποταπὰ τὰ ἀόρατα; Εἰ οὐρανοῦ μέγεθος μέτρον ἀνθρωπίνης διανοίας ἐκβαίνει, τῶν ἀϊδίων τὴν φύσιν τίς ἄρα νοῦς ἐξιχνιάσαι δυνήσεται; Εἰ ὁ τῇ φθορᾷ ὑποκείμενος ἥλιος οὕτω καλὸς, οὕτω μέγας, ὀξὺς μὲν κινηθῆναι, εὐτάκτους δὲ τὰς περιόδους ἀποδιδοὺς, σύμμετρον μὲν ἔχων τὸ μέγεθος τῷ παντὶ, ὥστε μὴ ἐκβαίνειν τὴν πρὸς τὸ ὅλον ἀναλογίαν· τῷ δὲ κάλλει τῆς φύσεως οἷόν τις ὀφθαλμὸς διαυγὴς ἐμπρέπων τῇ κτίσει· εἰ ἀκόρεστος τούτου ἡ θέα, ποταπὸς τῷ κάλλει ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος; Εἰ τυφλῷ ζημία τοῦτον μὴ βλέπειν, ποταπὴ ζημία τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ τοῦ ἀληθινοῦ φωτὸς στερηθῆναι; 6.2 Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ εἰς φαῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὥστε διαχωρίζειν ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτός. Οὐρανὸς προειλήφει καὶ γῆ· τὸ φῶς ἐπὶ τούτοις δεδημιούργητο· ἡμέρα καὶ νὺξ διεκέκριτο· πάλιν στερέωμα, καὶ ξηρᾶς φανέρωσις. Τὸ ὕδωρ συνήθροιστο εἰς συνεστηκυῖαν καὶ ἀφωρισμένην συναγωγήν. Ἡ γῆ πεπλήρωτο τοῖς οἰκείοις γεννήμασι, τά τε μυρία γένη τῶν βοτανῶν ἐκβλαστή σασα, καὶ παντοδαποῖς εἴδεσι φυτῶν εὐθηνουμένη. Ἥλιος δὲ οὔπω ἦν καὶ σελήνη, ἵνα μήτε φωτὸς ἀρχηγὸν καὶ πατέρα τὸν ἥλιον ὀνομάσωσι· μήτε τῶν ἐκ τῆς γῆς φυομένων δημιουργὸν, οἱ τὸν Θεὸν ἀγνοήσαντες ἡγήσωνται. Διὰ τοῦτο τετάρτη ἡμέρα· καὶ τότε εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς, Γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. Ὅταν τὸν εἰπόντα διδαχθῇς, εὐθὺς τῇ ἐννοίᾳ σύναπτε τὸν ἀκούσαντα. Εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς, Γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες, καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τοὺς δύο φωστῆρας. Τίς εἶπε καὶ τίς ἐποίησεν; Οὐκ ἐννοεῖς ἐν τούτοις τὸ διπλοῦν τῶν προσώπων; Πανταχοῦ τῇ ἱστορίᾳ τὸ δόγμα τῆς θεολογίας μυστικῶς συμπαρέσπαρται. Καὶ ἡ χρεία πρόσκειται τῆς τῶν φωστήρων γενέσεως· Εἰς φαῦσιν, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Εἰ προειλήφει τοῦ φωτὸς ἡ γένεσις, πῶς νῦν ὁ ἥλιος πάλιν εἰς φαῦσιν λέγεται γεγονέναι; Πρῶτον μὲν οὖν τῆς λέξεως τὸ ἰδιότροπον μηδένα σοι κινείτω γέλωτα, εἴπερ μὴ ἑπόμεθα ταῖς παρ' ὑμῖν ἐκλογαῖς τῶν ῥημάτων, μηδὲ τὸ τῆς θέσεως αὐτῶν εὔρυθμον ἐπιτηδεύομεν. Οὐ γὰρ τορευταὶ λέξεων παρ' ἡμῖν· οὐδὲ τὸ εὔηχον τῶν φωνῶν, ἀλλὰ τὸ εὔσημον τῶν ὀνομάτων πανταχοῦ προτιμότερον. Σκόπει τοίνυν εἰ μὴ διὰ τῆς φαύσεως ἀρκούντως ἐνέφηνεν ὃ ἐβούλετο· ἀντὶ γὰρ τοῦ φωτισμοῦ τὴν φαῦσιν εἴρηκεν. Ἔστι δὲ οὐδὲν μαχόμενον τοῦτο τοῖς περὶ τοῦ φωτὸς εἰρημένοις. Τότε μὲν γὰρ αὐτὴ τοῦ φωτὸς ἡ φύσις παρήχθη· νῦν δὲ τὸ ἡλιακὸν τοῦτο σῶμα ὄχημα εἶναι τῷ πρωτογόνῳ ἐκείνῳ φωτὶ παρεσκεύασται.
thought_title: Man lifted toward heaven and the lights of the fourth day
orientation: Basil finishes urging his hearers to know themselves and then starts explaining the fourth day of creation.
pass_a_gloss: ...being made less in the equipments from nature, but by the abundance of reason able to be lifted above toward heaven. If we learn these things, we shall recognize ourselves, we shall know God, worship the one who founded, serve the Master, glorify the Father, love our nourisher, revere the benefactor, not cease worshipping the author of our life present and to come, the one making faithful through the wealth he already provided also the things in promises, and by the experience of present things confirming to us the things expected. For if the temporary things are such, of what kind are the eternal? And if the things seen are so fine, of what kind the unseen? If the size of heaven exceeds the measure of human thought, who then will be able to track out the nature of the everlasting things? If the sun subject to corruption is so fine, so great, swift to be moved, but rendering ordered circuits, having size proportioned to the all so as not to exceed the ratio toward the whole, and by the beauty of nature like some clear eye being conspicuous in creation; if the sight of it is insatiable, of what kind in beauty is the sun of righteousness? If loss to a blind man not to see this one, what kind of loss to the sinner to be deprived of the true light? And God said: let there come to be luminaries in the firmament of heaven for shining upon the earth, so as to separate between the day and between the night. Heaven had come first and earth; light upon these had been crafted; day and night had been distinguished; again firmament, and manifestation of dry land. The water had been gathered into a constituted and delimited gathering. The earth had been filled with its own produce, having sprouted the countless kinds of herbs and thriving with all sorts of forms of plants. But sun was not yet and moon, so that those ignorant of God would neither name the sun author and father of light nor consider it craftsman of the things growing from earth. Through this the fourth day; and then God said, Let luminaries come to be in the firmament of heaven. When you are taught the one who spoke, at once in thought join the one who heard. God said, Let luminaries come to be, and God made the two luminaries. Who said and who made? Do you not perceive in these the doubleness of the persons? Everywhere the doctrine of theology is mystically sown along with the history. And the use of the genesis of the luminaries is added: for shining, he says, upon the earth. If the genesis of light came before, how is the sun now again said to have come to be for shining? First then let the peculiarity of the wording move no laughter for you, if we do not follow the selections of words among you, nor practise the good rhythm of their placing. For there are no carvers of words among us; nor the good-sounding of the voices, but the clear-signifying of the names everywhere preferable. Consider then whether through 'shining' he did not show sufficiently what he wished; for instead of 'illumination' he has said 'shining'. This is nothing fighting with the things said about light. For then the very nature of light was brought forth; now this solar body has been prepared to be a vehicle for that first-born light.

pass_b_english: … falling short in the equipment that nature gives, but able through the wealth of reason to be lifted up to heaven. If we learn these things, we shall know ourselves, we shall come to know God, we shall worship the Creator, we shall serve the Master, we shall glorify the Father, we shall love our provider, we shall revere our benefactor, and we shall not cease to worship the author of our present and our future life, who through the wealth he has already given makes his promises sure, and by our experience of present things makes firm for us the things we hope for.

For if the things of time are such, what are the eternal things like? And if the visible things are so beautiful, what are the invisible things like? If the greatness of heaven goes beyond the measure of human thought, what mind will be able to trace out the nature of the everlasting things?

If the sun, which is subject to decay, is so beautiful, so great, swift in its motion yet keeping its circuits in good order, with a size so proportioned to the whole that it does not exceed its due ratio to the universe, and by the beauty of its nature standing out in creation like a bright eye; if the sight of it never satisfies, how beautiful must the Sun of righteousness be (Malachi 4:2)? If it is a loss for a blind man not to see this sun, what a loss it is for the sinner to be deprived of the true light!

“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven for shining upon the earth, to divide between the day and between the night” (Genesis 1:14). Heaven and earth had come first; light had been made after them; day and night had been separated; then the firmament, and the appearing of the dry land. The water had been gathered into a fixed and bounded gathering. The earth had been filled with its own offspring, having sprouted the countless kinds of herbs and flourishing with every form of plant. But there was not yet a sun, nor a moon, so that those who do not know God would neither call the sun the source and father of light nor think it the maker of the things that grow from the earth. That is why it is the fourth day; and then God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven.”

When you have been taught who spoke, join to him at once in your thought the one who heard. “God said, Let there be lights,” and “God made the two lights” (Genesis 1:16). Who spoke, and who made? Do you not perceive in these words the two persons? Everywhere in the history the doctrine of theology is mystically sown along with it. The use for which the lights came to be is also added: “For shining,” he says, “upon the earth.” If the coming to be of light had come first, how is the sun now said to have come to be, again, for shining? First, then, let the oddness of the wording move none of you to laughter, if we do not follow your choices of words or study a good rhythm in placing them. For among us there are no carvers of phrases; it is not the pleasant sound of words but the clear sense of terms that we everywhere prefer. See, then, whether by “shining” he has not shown well enough what he meant; for he said “shining” instead of “illumination”. And this is in no way at odds with what was said about light. For then the very nature of light was brought forth; now this body of the sun has been prepared to be a vehicle for that first-born light.

Retranslated clause by clause (alert item 9).

last_rejected.quote: and then, Basil says, God said
last_rejected.why: The English adds 'Basil says', which is not in the source. It also confuses who is speaking, since the next words are God's, quoted from Genesis.
last_rejected.fix: For this reason the fourth day came, and only then did God say, "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven."
last_rejected.ruling: καὶ τότε εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς still rendered as God said; added Basil says leaves speaker intact

last_rejected.quote: Basil asks you to see in this doubling the two persons.
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐκ ἐννοεῖς ἐν τούτοις τὸ διπλοῦν τῶν προσώπων;
last_rejected.why: The source is a direct rhetorical question to the reader, with no named speaker. The English adds 'Basil' and turns the question into a statement.
last_rejected.fix: Do you not see in this the twofold persons?
